clusters.title: RL-tuned small models beat far larger untuned models, mainly by fixing tool-use behavior
clusters.idea: RL post-training on a small model closes or reverses the gap to models 10-100x larger, from InstructGPT's RLHF results to GRPO on 4B models for finance/SQL tasks. Recent talks locate the gain in behavioral discipline (inspecting schemas, not repeating failed queries) rather than knowledge, and stress how cheap it is (hundreds of dollars).

clusters.title: Fine-tune a small specialist only when economics or quality demand it
clusters.idea: Whether to replace frontier-model prompting with a tuned small model. Some talks treat it as an economics decision that small open models now win on cost and latency (Ramp, AT&T, a 95%-small-model routing target); others call fine-tuning a last resort that carries ongoing debt and should wait until a mature narrow application hits API limits.

clusters.title: Production traces should become continual training signal for agents
clusters.idea: Benchmarks saturate while production interactions are wasted; turn failed sessions, user feedback and process traces into SFT, distillation and RL data, and run it as a retrain-and-redeploy flywheel. Talks differ on the loop shape (outer feedback loop vs inner eval-climbing loop) and on the risks they flag: distribution shift, reward hacking, off-policy staleness.

clusters.title: Agent post-training is bottlenecked on realistic, replayable RL environments, not algorithms
clusters.idea: The scarce resource for agent RL is environments that reproduce production conditions: real web tasks, cloud provisioning and live traffic, simulated tools, replayable orchestrator-plus-sandbox setups, and the rollout infrastructure to run them in parallel. Talks differ on whether to simulate the world or bring your own production harness.

clusters.title: Define an RL environment once and reuse it for evals, RL, SFT and distillation
clusters.idea: An environment is a package of tasks, harness/interaction rules and a verifier/reward; built once, it scores models and produces training signal, so post-training becomes an iterate loop of build, score, read rollouts, train, deploy.

clusters.title: Curriculum and difficulty design shape what RL learns
clusters.idea: Task difficulty (opponent strength, progressively harder exploit targets) and reward design determine whether RL learns; build a graded, reproducible curriculum and watch for instability from batch size and temperature.

clusters.title: RL works where outcomes are automatically verifiable, so turn tasks into verifiable ones
clusters.idea: Code, search, OCR and similar domains train well because execution or reference checks give strict deterministic rewards (Verifier's Law); preference reward models are comparatively easy to game. The prescription is to convert fuzzy domains into context-specific verifiable tasks.

clusters.title: Rewards without ground truth (LLM judges, human preference) are needed but fragile
clusters.idea: Most real agent tasks have no golden answer, so rewards come from judges, rubrics or rater preference; these invite reward hacking and optimize for what pleases raters (chatty assistants) rather than reliable action. Task difficulty must be calibrated to keep such rewards informative.

clusters.title: Dense, richer-than-scalar learning signals beat sparse rewards
clusters.idea: Token-level on-policy self-distillation and LLM reflection over full traces and textual feedback give denser credit assignment than scalar RLHF/GRPO rewards, avoiding reward-shaping regressions and improving sample efficiency.

clusters.title: Generate training tasks synthetically, then filter hard: task fidelity beats task count
clusters.idea: Build RL/SFT tasks programmatically from real structured sources (SEC tables, Wikidata random walks), overproduce and filter via programmatic checks, verifiers and expert review. Controlled results show high-fidelity tasks and verifier-filtered trajectories beat larger lower-quality sets.

clusters.title: Invest in data curation pipelines before scaling compute
clusters.idea: Better data steepens scaling laws: dedupe, quality-filter, resample to the task distribution, caption and tag at scale, and check coverage. Talks cover text reasoning data (OpenThoughts), pretraining mixes and billion-image datasets, often distilling a large model into a cheap filter.

clusters.title: Synthetic data: complement to organic data or a threat to diversity
clusters.idea: One view: synthetic rephrasing regularizes presentation, fills under-represented formats and beats seeds-only training, while hard quality filters backfire through repetition. The opposing view avoids synthetic training images to preserve unconventional styles and aesthetic diversity.

clusters.title: Distil a slow strong model into a small fast student for the narrow task
clusters.idea: Use a frontier model or VLM as teacher/labeler, repair or review its outputs, and train a small low-latency model to deploy instead; watch for judge disagreement and wrong augmentations.

clusters.title: Coding agents can run the fine-tuning workflow themselves
clusters.idea: Agents with skills/MCP can pick data, configure and launch fine-tuning jobs from a plain-language request, hill-climb against evals with synthetic data, and increasingly automate parts of ML research.

clusters.title: Continual learning is a design space: pick the layer and data regime per failure
clusters.idea: Agents can be improved in weights, harness or memory, from offline or on-policy data, via SFT, RL, LoRA or prompt optimization. Talks propose axes (replayability, lifelongness, efficiency; hints vs traces) for picking per failure, with regression-gated replayable environments.

clusters.title: Fine-tune tiny models for narrow on-device tasks and measure on the target hardware
clusters.idea: A tiny model fine-tuned (often on synthetic data) for one function-calling or agent task can go from unreliable to ~90% accurate on devices like a Raspberry Pi; quantization, runtime choice, small guardrail models and memory limits must be tuned on the actual device.

clusters.title: Spend offline compute to move a private corpus into the model
clusters.idea: Models lack post-cutoff, long-tail and private knowledge; spend compute offline on the corpus (sleep-time compute) and transfer it via KV compaction or on-policy distillation.

clusters.title: Pretraining is being reshaped to produce good RL starting points
clusters.idea: Pretraining mixes shift toward code, reasoning and long-context agent data, and SFT-style examples move earlier, so base models are built for post-training.

clusters.title: Train text and vision together from the first step
clusters.idea: Bolting vision onto a pretrained text model degrades text ability or is fragile; joint multimodal training from scratch nearly preserves text performance.

clusters.title: Faithful population simulation needs real-distribution training, not persona prompts or preference tuning
clusters.idea: Fine-tuning on real survey response distributions matches populations better than persona prompting, while preference optimization can make persona outputs more pleasing but less faithful (concealing anachronism).

clusters.title: LLM recommenders over semantic item IDs
clusters.idea: Represent catalog items as semantic IDs so an LLM natively generates recommendations, training on language plus catalog data in stages that keep language steerability.

clusters.title: Pretrain a foundation model on transaction sequences
clusters.idea: Next-transaction prediction over billions of transactions, with tokenization of amounts, time gaps and locations as the central challenge; it needed more tokens per parameter than Chinchilla and beat an XGBoost fraud baseline.

clusters.title: Frontier VLMs pattern-match instead of reasoning visually; fixing needs specialized data
clusters.idea: Counting, spatial grounding and video state tracking fail; scale alone won't fix it, specialized and synthetic data, architecture changes and visual chain of thought will.

clusters.title: Learn training fundamentals by training a tiny GPT from scratch
clusters.idea: A ~10M-parameter GPT on a laptop teaches tokenizer, architecture, LR schedule and overfitting; sanity-check initial loss against uniform-over-vocab and watch train/val divergence.

clusters.title: Cascaded STT-LLM-TTS pipelines vs native speech-to-speech and full-duplex models
clusters.idea: One camp says cascades are half-duplex walkie-talkies that lose paralinguistic cues and latency, so native audio and full-duplex models (Moshi, Gemini Live, joint audio-video-text models) are required. Others hold that open cascaded stacks are good enough now, and single multimodal calls already replace multi-service batch audio pipelines.

clusters.title: In voice, latency beats IQ: a small fast talker with reasoning moved elsewhere
clusters.idea: A one-second pause feels broken and a smarter answer doesn't compensate, so voice turns go to small low-latency models. Hard work moves out of the talking model into state machines, background text LLMs or per-turn routing, at the cost of strict guardrails against drift.

clusters.title: Hide voice latency by streaming and overlapping every stage
clusters.idea: Use true streaming STT, start TTS while the LLM is still streaming, transcribe speculatively, run tools asynchronously, play cached prefixes and colocate models, optimizing perceived rather than total latency.

clusters.title: Measure audible response time from the user's last syllable, against human turn-taking norms
clusters.idea: Humans switch turns in ~200 ms; ~600 ms feels human and ~1.5 s is the edge of conversational. Dashboard latency misleads because TTS leading silence and first-sentence time dominate.

clusters.title: Turn detection and interruption handling make or break voice agents
clusters.idea: Layer audio-aware turn classifiers (rhythm, pitch, intonation) over VAD or provider endpointing, and cancel in-flight LLM/TTS output immediately on barge-in; measured cutoffs halved (4.5% vs 9.9%) at equal latency.

clusters.title: Judge voice agents end-to-end on real audio and outcomes, not component scores or transcripts
clusters.idea: Component leaderboards and clean transcripts hide dead air, overlap, mishearing and confirmed-but-never-executed actions; benchmark the whole stack with simulated callers, link audio to tool traces, and verify downstream side effects across interdependent layers.

clusters.title: Voice-captured data is structured extraction: schema up front, confirm before sync
clusters.idea: Treat call data like a typed form with field-level evaluation; LLM summarization and extraction cut after-call work, with PII masked early, channels kept separate, and operator confirmation before CRM sync.

clusters.title: Open-weight TTS is now viable for real-time and on-device voice
clusters.idea: Small open TTS models run on CPU, reach sub-200 ms first-token latency and clone voices from short samples, removing cloud cost and latency.

clusters.title: Direct synthetic voices with natural-language descriptions
clusters.idea: Prompt TTS for style, emotion and accent, or generate a character voice from a text description of era, culture and personality.

clusters.title: Add voice as an interface layer over an agent's existing tools
clusters.idea: Keep the agent's orchestration, retrieval and tools, and add speech in/out around it; voice can trigger tools mid-conversation and need not always talk back (speech-to-action, event-to-speech).

clusters.title: Speaker diarization matters for transcripts fed to LLMs
clusters.idea: Plain STT loses who spoke and overlaps; combine diarization with transcripts and measure it with DER.

clusters.title: Don't trust generic ASR transcripts: domain-tune or clean them before acting
clusters.idea: Generic ASR fails on domain terms like drug names; fine-tune it or clean unreliable transcripts before the agent acts.

clusters.title: Robotics follows the LLM recipe: generalist pretraining on video and simulation, then teleop post-training
clusters.idea: One embodied foundation model across bodies, pretrained on web/human/gameplay video or simulation with sparse supervision, post-trained with teleoperation. Talks differ on the video vs teleop tradeoff and on where training video comes from.

clusters.title: Physical-world reliability: learned policies with failure-targeted data vs modular tool-based autonomy
clusters.idea: Demos are easy, reliability is hard. One approach fine-tunes generalist policies and uses reward models to target recovery data at failures; others keep modular edge/cloud autonomy and let LLM/VLM agents pick among existing robot tools. Both feed fleet data back into models.
